impact_assessment.why: Peak normalization can leave a quiet-sounding track at full peak; loudness work needs an RMS target mode.
impact_assessment.benefits: normalize --rms-target <dBFS> scales a Coda WAV to a chosen RMS level with deterministic clamping, complementing peak mode.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: silence must be left unchanged, invalid dBFS targets must fail clearly, and peak mode must stay byte-identical; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure RMS gain function with known-vector and silence tests, extend the normalize CLI, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.
